The page also states a total indicative tuition fee for 2027 commencement of AU$107,520 (2-year plan MC199P15) and AU$80,160 (1.5-year plan); the page markup did not clearly label these totals as international, though they are consistent with the international annual rate. SSAF AU$386 is the 2027 maximum. 22 Oct 2026 re-check: tuition is now the page's own indicative 2-year total of AU$107,520, because 2 x AU$52,800 = AU$105,600 does not match it (likely fee indexation in year two). The page does not label the total as international and does not explain the gap, so this stays 'partial'.

living_cost.basis: budget = Home Affairs Student visa financial-capacity living-cost figure of AUD 29,710 for 12 months for a student, divided by 12 (official minimum, not a realistic city budget). moderate = ESTIMATE: midpoint of RMIT's published 2026 Melbourne living-expense range AUD 30,000-45,000 per year (37,500 / 12). comfortable = ESTIMATE: top of that RMIT range (45,000 / 12). Sydney is typically dearer; no official 2026 Sydney figure found.

fees.label: Main applicant visa application charge (from 1 July 2026; was AUD 2,000)
Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) application charge, from 1 July 2026 (was AUD 4,600)

proof_of_funds.text: Show enough money for 12 months: living costs AUD 29,710 for the student (partner AUD 10,394, child AUD 4,449, now only for exempt categories), plus first 12 months of course fees (less amounts already paid), plus travel of AUD 2,000 if applying from outside Australia (India). Alternative: evidence that parents or partner earned at least AUD 87,856 personal annual income in the 12 months before applying (combined income of both parents can count), shown via official government documents such as tax assessments. Example: Monash MDS year 1 = 57,540 + 29,710 + 2,000 = about AUD 89,250. Genuine Student requirement: answer GS questions in the online application (150-word limit each) showing study is the primary reason for the visa. English: approved test taken within 2 years; online/at-home tests (e.g. IELTS Online, TOEFL Home Edition) are not accepted.

work_during_study.text: Up to 48 hours a fortnight while the course is in session (rules for course breaks not captured from the page; check your visa grant conditions). No work before the course starts. Master's by research and doctoral students have no work limit; master's by coursework students are subject to the 48-hour cap.

post_study_work.name: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream
post_study_work.text: Open work rights; you find your own job. Default stays: Bachelor 2 years, Masters (coursework and extended) 2 years, Masters (research) 3 years, Doctoral 3 years. For Indian nationals under the Australia-India ECTA (AI-ECTA): Masters (coursework, extended and research) 3 years, PhD 4 years, Bachelor 2 years (3 with first-class honours in STEM incl. ICT). Must be aged 35 or under when applying (exceptions for masters by research/PhD, HK/BNO up to 50), have held a Student visa in the last 6 months, and have a CRICOS degree awarded in the last 6 months. English for tests on/after 7 Aug 2025: e.g. IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, PTE Academic 55. Cannot be extended; a second Post-Higher Education Work stream may be available in limited cases. Application charge AUD 5,750 from 1 July 2026.

pr_pathway.text: Points-tested Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189): occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list, suitable skills assessment, Expression of Interest in SkillSelect, aged under 45 at invitation, at least 65 points (invitations may require more), invitation-only. Employer route: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) Core Skills stream needs a sponsoring employer, an occupation on the Core Skills Occupation List, salary at least the market rate and not less than the Core Skills Income Threshold, and at least 1 year relevant work experience; this can later lead to employer-sponsored permanent residence (subclass 186 details not verified in this pass). State-nominated (190) and regional (491) routes also exist (not verified here).

recent_changes.title: Student visa application charge raised from AUD 2,000 to AUD 2,500
recent_changes.who_affected: All Student visa primary applicants except ASEAN, Pacific Island/Timor-Leste passport holders and independent ELICOS/non-award students
recent_changes.impact: Indian applicants pay AUD 2,500 per application, about 25% more. Small next to tuition, but it is the latest of several rises.

recent_changes.title: Temporary Graduate (485) application charge raised from AUD 4,600 to AUD 5,750
recent_changes.who_affected: All 485 applicants except the Pacific Island/Timor-Leste concession
recent_changes.impact: Adds about AUD 1,150 to the cost of staying on to work after graduation.

recent_changes.title: Most Student visa applicants can no longer include family members; no subsequent entrants
recent_changes.who_affected: Student visa applications lodged on or after 2 October 2026, unless in an exemption category (reported exemptions include PhD students, government-scholarship holders, ASEAN/Pacific nationals)
recent_changes.impact: A typical Indian master's student cannot bring a spouse or child, and family cannot join later. A partner cannot earn alongside the student, which hurts household ROI for married applicants.

recent_changes.title: Most Student visa holders can no longer apply for a further Student visa onshore
recent_changes.who_affected: Current Student visa holders (and most temporary visa holders) wanting another Student visa, unless they meet an exemption
recent_changes.impact: Changing or extending courses in Australia now usually means applying from outside the country. Less flexibility if you fail units or want to switch courses.

recent_changes.title: Ministerial Direction 115 sets offshore Student visa processing priority (replaced MD111)
recent_changes.who_affected: Offshore Student visa applicants; priority depends on the provider's progress against its allocation
recent_changes.impact: If your university is near its allocation, your visa may be processed more slowly. Applying early and to providers with room matters. MD111 applied from 19 Dec 2024 to applications lodged before 14 Nov 2025.

recent_changes.title: National Planning Level for 2027 held at 295,000 new overseas student commencements
recent_changes.who_affected: New overseas students commencing in 2027; enforced through provider allocations and Ministerial Direction visa prioritisation
recent_changes.impact: A soft cap stays in place for 2027. Popular courses can fill up or close to new international students (UNSW already flags some 2026 programs at capacity).

recent_changes.title: Legislated international student enrolment caps (ESOS Amendment (Quality and Integrity) Bill 2024)
recent_changes.who_affected: Would have capped enrolments by provider
recent_changes.impact: The Senate did not pass the caps; the bill lapsed on 28 March 2025 and the caps part was left out of the later ELA Bill. The government uses Ministerial Directions and planning levels instead, so caps still exist in practice.

check.note: The cited government document did not respond on 22 Oct 2026, so the claim could not be re-checked.

recent_changes.title: Temporary Graduate visa realigned: age limit cut to 35, Post-Study Work stream renamed Post-Higher Education Work
recent_changes.impact: Applicants over 35 (coursework master's) cannot get a 485. Default coursework-master's stay is 2 years, but Indian nationals keep 3 years under AI-ECTA.

recent_changes.title: New English test score tables for tests taken on or after 7 August 2025
recent_changes.who_affected: Student and 485 applicants using English tests taken from 7 Aug 2025
recent_changes.impact: Check the current score table before booking a test. At-home/online tests are not accepted.

policy_volatility.evidence: In 24 months: MD111 (Dec 2024) then MD115 (Nov 2025) processing caps, planning levels, new English score tables (Aug 2025), two fee rises to AUD 2,500 (Jul 2026), and a ban on dependants and onshore re-applications (Oct 2026).

psw_uncertainty.evidence: The 485 is an open work visa with set lengths, and Indian master's graduates get 3 years under AI-ECTA. Risks: the age-35 cap, the AUD 5,750 fee, and 2024 cuts showing the rules can change.

work_restrictions.evidence: 48 hours a fortnight during term for coursework students. Unrestricted work on the 485. PR needs points (65+, invitation-only) or employer sponsorship.

funds_burden.evidence: Must show AUD 29,710 living costs, first-year tuition and AUD 2,000 travel (about AUD 75k-100k for these programmes), or parental income of at least AUD 87,856. Largely matches real first-year costs.

recent_adverse.evidence: Last 12 months: Student and 485 fees up 25% (Jul 2026), family members barred for most students and no onshore re-applications (Oct 2026), 2027 cap held at 295,000.

CS.basis: QILT Graduate Outcomes Survey 2025, postgraduate coursework, Computing and information systems, median annual full-time salary. mid = INTERNATIONAL graduates total 2025 (AUD 65,200; 2024 was 70,000). low = lowest international gender-cell median 2025 (female, 65,000). high = DOMESTIC postgraduate coursework graduates 2025 median (AUD 120,000), which includes many already-experienced workers, so treat it as an upside ceiling, not an entry figure. For an Indian graduate the international median is the realistic entry figure.
CS.source_name: QILT Graduate Outcomes Survey 2025 (International and National report tables)
CS.period: annual gross, AUD, GOS 2025 short-term graduate outcomes

DS.basis: QILT has no separate data science study area; data science is mapped here to Computing and information systems (same figures as CS). For reference, Science and mathematics international PGC 2025 median = AUD 64,400. mid = international median 2025; low = lowest international gender-cell 2025; high = domestic PGC median 2025 (upside ceiling, includes experienced workers).
DS.source_name: QILT Graduate Outcomes Survey 2025 (International and National report tables)
DS.period: annual gross, AUD, GOS 2025 short-term graduate outcomes

MBA.basis: QILT GOS 2025, postgraduate coursework, narrow area Business management (within Business and management). mid = international graduates 2025 median (AUD 66,000; broad Business and management = 65,000). low = lowest international gender-cell 2025 (female, 65,400). high = domestic PGC Business management median 2025 (AUD 140,000), which reflects mostly experienced domestic MBA graduates, so it is an upside ceiling.
MBA.source_name: QILT Graduate Outcomes Survey 2025 (International and National report tables)
MBA.period: annual gross, AUD, GOS 2025 short-term graduate outcomes

tax.basis: ESTIMATE for a single Australian resident for tax purposes on about AUD 65,200 in 2026-27. Brackets: 0% to 18,200; 15% to 45,000; 30% to 135,000 (AUD 4,020 plus 30c per $1 over 45,000). Income tax = 10,080, plus 2% Medicare levy = 1,304, total 11,384 = 17.5%. Ignores the Low Income Tax Offset (about AUD 20 at this income) and the Medicare levy surcharge. At AUD 120,000 the same method gives about 24%. The 2026-27 15% bottom rate (down from 16%) is law per ATO/Budget material. ato.gov.au blocked automated access, so the table was read from SuperGuide (secondary, updated 1 July 2026; its 2025-26 table matches ATO 2025-26 rates). Medicare levy 2% is standard; not read on an ATO page.

health_insurance_per_year.basis: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), single student: midpoint of the AU$590-750 a year range on RMIT's cost page (2026); Medibank lists from AU$719. Varies by insurer. It is not included in living costs.

checklist: Check your course is CRICOS-registered and not at capacity for international intakes (planning-level allocations)
Apply to the university; accept the offer, pay the deposit and get your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)
Buy Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the whole visa period
Take an approved in-person English test (no at-home tests) within 2 years of lodging
Prepare financial evidence: AUD 29,710 living + year-1 tuition + AUD 2,000 travel, or parental income of at least AUD 87,856
Draft Genuine Student answers (150 words each) on why this course, provider and Australia
Create an ImmiAccount and lodge the subclass 500 application from India; pay AUD 2,500
Book biometrics at a VFS centre when asked, and complete the health exam with a panel physician
After grant, check visa conditions in VEVO (48 hours per fortnight work limit; no family members unless exempt)
Plan your 485 early: apply within 6 months of completion, aged 35 or under, with a new English test and the AUD 5,750 fee
